en.headline: Two men jailed for up to 38 months over secession conspiracy
en.dek: District Court sentenced a courier and a waiter who admitted conspiracy to commit secession after joining a Taiwan-based group advocating Hong Kong independence; the judge said their actions risked social stability.
body: Two men were sentenced in the District Court on Thursday to terms of 38 months and 36 months after admitting conspiracy to commit secession under the national security law.

Chan Tai-sum, 27, a courier, and Ng Chi-tung, 25, a waiter, had pleaded guilty to taking part in the Hong Kong Democratic Independence Union between November 2024 and July 2025. The group, founded by a wanted person, advocated Hong Kong independence and related goals. A third co-defendant, a student, was sentenced earlier to 42 months.

Judge Ernest Lin Kam-hung said the pair had acted as advisers, helping design materials and plans. He noted Chan’s previous conviction for related offences and described the conduct as harmful to social stability and national unity. Both men had cited autism diagnoses in mitigation; the judge said the condition did not prevent them understanding the nature of their actions.

zh.headline: 兩男認串謀分裂國家罪 分別判囚38個月及36個月
zh.dek: 區域法院周四判處兩名承認參與「香港民主建國聯盟」的男子監禁，法官指行為不利社會安定及國家統一；同案另一被告早前已判囚42個月。
body: 兩名男子周四在區域法院因承認《國安法》下串謀分裂國家罪，分別被判監禁38個月及36個月。
27歲速遞員陳泰森及25歲侍應伍始東，承認於2024年11月至2025年7月期間參與以推動香港獨立為宗旨的「香港民主建國聯盟」。該組織由通緝人士創立。同案另一名學生被告早前已認罪並被判囚42個月。
法官練錦鴻指兩人擔任顧問角色，協助設計宣傳材料及相關計劃。他指出陳泰森曾有相關前科，並認為其行為對香港社會安定及國家統一有負面影響。兩人求情時提及患有自閉症，法官認為該情況不影響他們理解行為性質。
